issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Course property/initializer parameter named `instructor`, but the solution repository uses `lecturer` as the stored property and initializer parameter name. This causes multiple structural mismatches in the solution: Client constructs a Course using the `instructor:` label (which does not match the solution's initializer), and Developer.swift in the solution references `course.instructor` (which does not exist in the solution's Course). This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct property/parameter name to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course API consistent across all artifacts. Preferably rename the solution's Course property and initializer parameter from `lecturer` to `instructor` (and update the initializer signature accordingly) so it matches the problem statement and the template. Alternatively, if `lecturer` is preferred, update the problem statement, the template, Client.swift and Developer.swift to use `lecturer` everywhere. Ensure property access in Developer.swift and the constructor call in Client.swift match the chosen name.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect the Course property and initializer parameter to be named 'instructor' (e.g. Course(name:..., instructor: ...), property 'instructor'). However, the solution implementation uses the identifier 'lecturer' for the same conceptual property in Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift. Meanwhile other solution files (Sources/DeveloperLib/Client.swift and Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift) still reference 'instructor'. This inconsistency (instructor vs. lecturer) breaks the one-to-one mapping students must make between the problem description and the code and will cause confusion and compilation errors when following the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the course instructor across all artifacts. Prefer matching the problem statement and template by renaming the solution's 'lecturer' property and initializer parameter to 'instructor', and update all references (in Developer.swift and Client.swift) accordingly so every artifact uses 'instructor' consistently.
